questions.question: If you are not sure how to put out a fire in your vehicle, what should you do?

options.text: Use water.
Stay inside the vehicle.
Wait for the firefighters.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait for the firefighters.
questions.explanation: If you do not know which type of fire extinguisher to use, wait for firefighters to arrive. They are trained to handle dangerous fires safely.

questions.question: When passing parked cars, a driver should:

options.text: Stay close to the vehicles.
Watch for people getting out of vehicles.
Flash their headlights.

questions.correctAnswerText: Watch for people getting out of vehicles.
questions.explanation: Be careful when passing parked cars. A person may step out without looking, or a driver may start their car without seeing you.

questions.question: A smaller vehicle compared to your vehicle:

options.text: Can usually stop faster than your vehicle.
Usually takes longer to stop than your vehicle.
Takes about the same time to stop as your vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can usually stop faster than your vehicle.
questions.explanation: Smaller vehicles can stop faster than larger vehicles. Remember this when deciding how far to stay behind other cars.

questions.question: When approaching a railroad crossing, a bus driver should:

options.text: Stop between 15 and 50 feet from the nearest track.
Drive carefully but only stop if a train is coming.
Speed up to cross the tracks quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop between 15 and 50 feet from the nearest track.
questions.explanation: Stop the bus 15 to 50 feet from the nearest track. Look both ways for a train before proceeding.

questions.question: Before a bus enters a curve, the driver should:

options.text: Speed up.
Keep the same speed.
Slow down.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down.
questions.explanation: Always enter curves at a slower speed. Be extra careful on wet or slippery roads.

questions.question: On a slippery surface, stopping distance:

options.text: Is longer than on a normal road.
Is shorter than on a normal road.
Is about the same as on a normal road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Is longer than on a normal road.
questions.explanation: Slippery surfaces have less grip, so it takes longer to stop your vehicle.

questions.question: To stay alert while driving, you should:

options.text: Eat a heavy meal before your trip.
Keep the cab warm.
Travel with another driver who can take turns driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Travel with another driver who can take turns driving.
questions.explanation: Sharing the driving keeps both drivers fresh and alert. Also avoid heavy foods and keep the cab cool to fight fatigue.

questions.question: The danger of looking at your mirrors too long is:

options.text: You will see potential hazards.
You will not see what is happening on the road ahead.
The mirrors may shake and move.

questions.correctAnswerText: You will not see what is happening on the road ahead.
questions.explanation: Watching mirrors too long means you miss seeing what is ahead of you. Always be aware of what is happening in all directions.

questions.question: When checking your tires, you do not want to find:

options.text: Tire tread that is 4/32 of an inch deep.
Valve stems without damage.
Mismatched tire sizes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Mismatched tire sizes.
questions.explanation: Front tires need at least 4/32 inch of tread. Other tires need at least 2/32 inch. Valve stems must not be cut or cracked. All tires should match in size.

questions.question: When returning to traffic after a bus stop, you should:

options.text: Assume other drivers will let you merge.
Wait for a gap large enough to safely accelerate and merge.
Have a passenger stop traffic to let you merge.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait for a gap large enough to safely accelerate and merge.
questions.explanation: A bus needs more space to merge than smaller vehicles. Wait for a large enough gap in traffic before moving back onto the road.

questions.question: A commercial motor vehicle should:

options.text: Not have a fire extinguisher unless it carries hazardous materials.
Not have a fire extinguisher unless it travels through remote areas.
Have a fire extinguisher and other emergency equipment.

questions.correctAnswerText: Have a fire extinguisher and other emergency equipment.
questions.explanation: All commercial motor vehicles must have emergency equipment. This includes spare fuses, three red reflective triangles or flares, and at least one fire extinguisher that is charged and ready to use.

questions.question: If an aggressive driver confronts you, you should:

options.text: Make eye contact.
Ignore their gestures.
Try to race.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ignore their gestures.
questions.explanation: Do not respond to an angry driver's gestures. Avoid looking at the other driver and do not try to race them.

questions.question: A truck tractor built after March 1, 1997 must have:

options.text: An Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS).
A flag.
Hydraulic brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: An Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS).
questions.explanation: Truck tractors with air brakes built on or after March 1, 1997 must have an Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS).

questions.question: A disruptive passenger should be:

options.text: Removed from the bus immediately, no matter where.
Let off at the next bus stop.
Kept on the bus and taken to the police department.

questions.correctAnswerText: Let off at the next bus stop.
questions.explanation: Bus drivers are responsible for passenger safety even if they are disruptive. The passenger should be let off at a safe place, such as the next scheduled stop or a well-lit area with other people present.

questions.question: Before inspecting your vehicle, you should look under it to check for:

options.text: Whether the vehicle is on an incline.
Fresh fluid leaks on the ground.
Whether the vehicle is in a parking spot.

questions.correctAnswerText: Fresh fluid leaks on the ground.
questions.explanation: Look under the vehicle for fresh leaks of oil, grease, or fuel. Also check around the vehicle for hazards like other vehicles, people, or low-hanging wires or tree limbs.

questions.question: Roads are especially slippery right after rain starts because:

options.text: Water mixes with oil and grease on the road.
Tires cannot grip in wet weather.
Water has not yet washed away dirt and grease.

questions.correctAnswerText: Water mixes with oil and grease on the road.
questions.explanation: When rain first starts, it creates a slick film by mixing with oil and grease on the road surface that has not yet washed away.

questions.question: If you doubt you have enough space to safely drive under a bridge or sign, you should:

options.text: Drive faster.
Drive more slowly.
Drive on the shoulder.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive more slowly.
questions.explanation: If you are not sure your vehicle will fit under an overhead object, slow down and take a different route if possible.

questions.question: To change lanes, you should:

options.text: Move quickly.
Move slowly and smoothly.
Hold down your horn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move slowly and smoothly.
questions.explanation: Always change lanes slowly and smoothly. This gives other drivers a chance to move or honk to alert you. Always signal when changing lanes.

questions.question: When visibility is poor, such as at dawn or dusk, you can increase your vehicle's visibility by:

options.text: Using your headlights.
Driving with your windows open.
Flashing your lights on and off.

questions.correctAnswerText: Using your headlights.
questions.explanation: When driving at dawn, dusk, or in bad weather, use your headlights on low beam to make your vehicle more visible.

questions.question: When stopping, you should apply the brake pedal by:

options.text: Pushing down gradually.
Pushing down quickly.
Pulling up gradually.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pushing down gradually.
questions.explanation: Push the brake pedal down gradually when stopping. Gradual braking helps you maintain control of your vehicle.
